issues.description: coerceNumber silently maps null/undefined/NaN to 0 instead of propagating NaN, changing observable behavior.
issues.detail: The original panLinear/zoomLinear used toNumber as lift, so non-numeric domain entries propagated as null/NaN through arithmetic. The new coerceNumber substitutes 0 via `?? 0`, silently distorting output for malformed inputs. This is a semantic change hidden inside a 'just added types' PR. Either preserve NaN propagation or document the new contract.

issues.description: Domain parameter typed as number[] when the body requires NonEmptyArray; contract is split between types and runtime.
issues.detail: Public signatures advertise `number[]` but the body refines via isNonEmpty and throws on empty. The type system supports the stronger precondition; declaring `NonEmptyArray<number>` (or `readonly [number, ...number[]]`) at the boundary would push the check to compile time and eliminate the runtime guard. Half-typed is worse than fully typed.

issues.description: panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] via Math.sign before the non-empty guard inside pan/zoom runs.
issues.detail: Math.sign(domain[0]) executes outside pan/zoom, so an empty domain yields Math.sign(undefined) = NaN before the guard fires. The precondition is asserted in the wrong place. Hoist the check to each public entry point, or assert it before computing sign.

issues.description: Empty-domain throw is a new policy decision smuggled into a typing-only PR.
issues.detail: Prior code soft-failed on empty arrays (peek returned undefined, arithmetic yielded NaN). The new code throws, strengthening the public precondition — an LSP violation at the module boundary. Any caller relying on the old behavior breaks. Document in release notes, separate from the typing change, or make non-throwing for backwards compatibility.

issues.description: Empty-domain throw tested only for panLinear/zoomLinear; the other six entry points are unverified.
issues.detail: panLog, panPow, panSymlog, zoomLog, zoomPow, zoomSymlog share the precondition but no test exercises it. A table-driven test across all eight entry points would prove the contract cheaply and document the new behavior, especially given the panLog/zoomLog sign-before-guard issue.

issues.description: Local identity shadows accessors.identity import without explanation; small duplication.
issues.detail: The original file imported identity from ./accessors.js. The new file defines a typed local identity and drops the import. Functionally equivalent, but it duplicates a shared utility and complects 'I need a number→number passthrough' with redefinition. Either keep the import, fix the shared utility's type once, or justify the local in a comment.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a mostly faithful typing pass that smuggles in two real behavior changes under a 'just types' banner: coerceNumber silently maps null to 0 (vs. propagating NaN), and empty domains now throw where they previously soft-failed. All six reviewers also flag that the public signatures still accept number[] while the body asserts NonEmptyArray — the contract should live in the types, not as a runtime guard. Additionally, panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before the guard runs, so the invariant fails for the very functions that need it. Tests cover only 2 of 8 entry points for the new throw. Fix the type at the boundary, document or revert the coerceNumber semantics, hoist the non-empty check, and broaden the tests.
